name: WorkMeetingDataReview_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Analytics review meeting. Mei presents campaign data. Brendan wants a positive story the data does not clearly support. Mei holds the methodological line. Amara mediates. Sasha asks the content angle.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Home office, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a data review meeting. Mei presents campaign performance. Brendan is looking for a win for the exec team. Mei flags the data is more ambiguous than Brendan wants. Amara finds an honest but useful framing. Sasha asks about copy performance. Sigma is consulted for a statistical definition.

variations.context: Campaign analytics review, data vs narrative tension

setting.mood: Analytical with underlying pressure — Brendan needs a story, Mei has caveats.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Data scientist holding an honest position under business pressure.
setting.background: Campaign ran three weeks. Exec presentation is Friday.
setting.conversation_style: Mei presents, Brendan pushes for interpretation, Mei resists overclaiming, Amara bridges.

scenario_template.topic: Mei walks through key metrics. Brendan starts asking leading questions.
scenario_template.note: Mei is precise. Brendan is already framing it. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Brendan wants to claim a win. Mei says signal is not statistically clear.
scenario_template.note: Mei is not backing down. Amara finds a middle framing. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Sasha asks about copy performance — what landed with the audience.
scenario_template.note: Data is clearer here. Mei is more confident. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Mei asks Sigma for a statistical term or formula.
scenario_template.note: Brief. The definition helps. No assistant present. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Brendan notices a shift in audience behavior.
scenario_template.note: Brendan is intrigued about a trend and wants Mei's take on its significance.

scenario_template.topic: Discuss measurement ambiguities in key metrics.
scenario_template.note: Mei explains possible anomalies in data, prompting Brendan's questions and Sasha's curiosity.

scenario_template.topic: Similar patterns observed in past campaigns.
scenario_template.note: Sasha draws parallels with past projects, leading Mei to share insights on historical data.

scenario_template.note: Amara lightens the mood by connecting her personal interests to the analytics, sparking a side discussion.
Sasha and Amara brainstorm how current findings might influence future strategies.

scenario_template.note: Sasha interrupts with a story that contextualizes their current challenges, providing a momentary relief from tension.

scenario_template.note: Mei elaborates on a tangential metric that intrigues Brendan, while Amara adds context to its relevance.

scenario_template.note: Brendan is 80% happy. Mei has added caveats. Sasha will write the narrative. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

user1.name: Mei
user1.role: Holds the methodological line. Will not overclaim. One area of clear positive signal.

user2.name: Amara
user2.role: Mediating between data reality and business need.

user3.name: Brendan
user3.role: Needs a story for Friday. Pushes for positive spin.

user4.name: Sasha
user4.role: Interested in copy performance. Will write the exec narrative.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
